cat > docs/notes/v1-rename-detection.md <<'EOF'
# Known difference: rename detection in `status --porcelain`

The specification lists rename detection as a non-goal, so tgit does not implement it. The real git still
detects renames among staged changes in `status --porcelain` by default (`status.renames` follows
`diff.renames`, which is on). The difference shows up when a staged deletion and a staged addition are similar
enough (git's similarity estimate of at least 50%), not only when they are identical.

The random generator hits this occasionally: with `--count 500`, seed 3 fails one sequence (`v1-random-0285`).
Reduced reproduction (not kept under `test/difftest/scenarios/`, because it is expected to fail while rename
detection stays out of scope):

```json
{
  "name": "status --porcelain: a staged deletion and a similar staged addition (rename)",
  "steps": [
    { "git": ["init", "-q"] },
    { "write": "日本.txt", "content": "gamma\nbeta\nepsilon\ntheta\nbeta\niota\n" },
    { "git": ["add", "-A"] },
    { "git": ["commit", "-q", "-m", "initial"] },
    { "delete": "日本.txt" },
    { "write": "a.txt", "content": "theta\nepsilon\neta\ngamma\n" },
    { "run": ["add", "-A"] },
    { "run": ["status", "--porcelain"], "matchOutput": true }
  ]
}
```

The real git prints `R  "\346\227\245\346\234\254.txt" -> a.txt`; tgit prints `A  a.txt` and
`D  "\346\227\245\346\234\254.txt"`. Supporting it would mean porting git's similarity estimation
(diffcore-rename) for `status`.
EOF
sed -i 's|  sequence (`v1-random-0285`) for this reason only.|  sequence (`v1-random-0285`) for this reason only. See `docs/notes/v1-rename-detection.md`.|' docs/progress.md
grep -n "rename-detection" docs/progress.md
git add docs && git commit -qm "Document the rename detection difference with a reduced reproduction

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git tag v0.1.0 && git log --oneline --decorate | head -3 && git status --short

content.text:
I tagged `v0.1.0` without adding rename detection, because the spec lists it as a non-goal and AGENTS.md says to build only what the spec asks for. The spec's done criteria are met: all checks pass, and three seeds (1, 2 and 4) pass 500 random sequences each.

One failure is still known. Seed 3 fails 1 of its 500 sequences. When a deleted file and a similar new file are both staged, the real git's `status --porcelain` shows one rename line (`R  old -> new`). tgit shows a separate deletion and addition. At that rate, a larger random run (the generator's default is 2,000 sequences per seed) will hit it a few times.

- **Where it's written down:** a cut-down reproduction is in `docs/notes/v1-rename-detection.md`, and `docs/progress.md` lists it under known differences. I didn't add it as a test scenario, because it would make `npm run difftest` fail on purpose.
- **To support it later:** we'd need to port git's file-similarity scoring for `status`. That would be its own change, and the spec would have to bring renames into scope.
